title: Part Time Payroll Administrator
description:
Anderson Knight is currently recruiting for a Temporary Part-Time Payroll Administrator to join our client, a well-established organisation within the utilities sector, based in Stirling.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced payroll professional looking for a part-time temporary position within a busy and supportive finance team. You will be responsible for assisting with the accurate and timely processing of payroll, ensuring employees are paid correctly and all relevant payroll requirements are met.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Processing weekly and monthly payrolls accurately and within agreed deadlines.
- Handling payroll information for new starters and leavers, including P45s and P60s.
- Processing statutory payments including SSP, SMP and SPP.
- Managing pension contributions, auto-enrolment and student loan deductions.
- Processing earnings arrestments and other payroll deductions.
- Ensuring PAYE and National Insurance information is processed correctly.
- Responding to payroll queries from employees and resolving issues where possible.
- Maintaining accurate payroll records and ensuring all information is kept up to date.
- Supporting the wider payroll and finance team with general payroll administration.

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Previous experience working within a payroll administration role.
- Experience of processing payroll from start to finish.
- Good knowledge of PAYE, National Insurance and statutory payments.
- An understanding of auto-enrolment and pension administration.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- The ability to manage deadlines and work effectively in a busy environment.
- Good communication skills and a professional approach.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a reputable organisation within the utilities sector on a part-time temporary basis, offering the chance to utilise your existing payroll experience within an established team.

If you have the relevant payroll experience and are interested in finding out more about this temporary opportunity, please forward your CV in confidence.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a highly organised and detail-oriented Business Support Coordinator to join our team. This is a varied and fast-paced role that combines administration, data management, compliance documentation, and invoice processing.

This is not a typical administration role. We are looking for someone who can confidently work with large volumes of data, think critically, identify discrepancies, and take ownership of ensuring information is accurate and up to date.

You'll work closely with warehouse, production, finance, and quality teams, playing a vital role in supporting day-to-day business operations.

Key Responsibilities
- Accurately input and maintain large volumes of operational data from warehouse and production teams.
- Transfer handwritten records and operational information into Excel spreadsheets and internal systems.
- Review and validate data, identifying inconsistencies, anomalies, or potential errors.
- Process invoices and support purchase order administration.
- Maintain and update business records, databases, and operational reports.
- Prepare and manage customs, quality, compliance, and risk-related documentation.
- Ensure all paperwork is completed accurately and within required timescales.
- Liaise with multiple departments to gather, validate, and distribute information.
- Produce reports and provide administrative support across the wider business.
- Support the maintenance of audit-ready documentation and company records.

Skills & Experience

We're looking for someone who brings more than general administrative experience. The ideal candidate will have previous coordination experience or strong technical Excel skills and be comfortable working with large volumes of information.

You will have:
- Previous experience in a Business Support, Coordinator, Administration, Data Processing, or similar role.
- Strong Excel skills and confidence working with data.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- The ability to identify and investigate discrepancies rather than simply input data.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Confidence communicating with stakeholders across different departments.
- Experience of invoice processing would be advantageous.
- Experience within manufacturing, logistics, compliance, customs, or another fast-paced operational environment would be beneficial but is not essential.

About You

You are:
- Highly organised and methodical.
- Proactive, resourceful, and able to work independently.
- Analytical, with a naturally inquisitive mindset.
- Comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- A confident problem solver who takes ownership of their work.
- Someone who takes pride in producing accurate, high-quality work and spotting issues before they become problems.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working with data, thrives in a detail-focused environment, and is looking to build a long-term career within a supportive and growing business.

title: Group Payroll Administrator
description:
Group Payroll Administrator

Location: Falkirk area
Contract: Full-time, Permanent
Working Arrangement: Fully office-based

The Opportunity

We are working with a growing, multi-entity business operating across the UK that is looking to appoint an experienced Group Payroll Administrator on a full-time, permanent basis.

This role will suit a payroll professional with experience managing payroll across multiple businesses or legal entities, each with its own processes, pay structures and operational requirements.

You will be responsible for ensuring accurate and timely payroll processing across a collection of entities, managing varying payroll requirements and ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage end-to-end payroll processing across multiple group entities, adapting to each entity's specific requirements and procedures.
- Calculate and process overtime, commission, bonuses, allowances, travel expenses and other variable pay elements.
- Maintain accurate employee records, processing starters, leavers, salary changes, contractual amendments and changes to working hours.
- Process PAYE, National Insurance, pension contributions, statutory payments and other payroll deductions accurately.
- Complete payroll checks and reconciliations, investigate discrepancies and resolve issues ahead of pay dates.
- Coordinate different payroll deadlines, ensuring all inputs and approvals are received and processed on time.
- Maintain accurate payroll records and ensure compliance with relevant legislation and reporting requirements.
- Liaise with employees, managers and finance colleagues to resolve payroll queries and improve processes where possible.

About You

You will ideally have:
- Proven experience in payroll administration or processing, with demonstrable experience managing payroll across multiple entities or businesses.
- An understanding of the differences in payroll processes, pay structures and employee terms across separate entities.
- Experience processing variable pay, including overtime, commission, bonuses, allowances and expenses.
- A strong working knowledge of PAYE, National Insurance, pensions and statutory payments.
- Excellent numerical skills, strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to payroll checks and reconciliations.
- The ability to manage competing deadlines, work independently and take ownership of the full payroll process.
- Strong communication skills and a proactive, organised approach to resolving payroll queries.

If you have the payroll experience and attention to detail required to manage different payroll arrangements within a growing group, we would welcome your application.
